name: bottom-up-bond-scout
description: Randomly chooses an object from the workspace (weighted by intra-string salience), picks a neighbor, selects a bond facet, determines descriptors and bond category, and proposes a bond between them if compatible.
execute_body:
# Bottom-up bond scout: choose object, neighbor, propose bond
from server.engine.workspace_objects import Letter

obj = choose_object('intra')
if obj is None:
    fizzle()

neighbor = choose_neighbor(obj)
if neighbor is None:
    fizzle()

# Scheme: `choose-bond-facet` (bonds.ss:196, 475-487) -- the facets both objects
# carry a description on, weighted by `description-type-support`
# (workspace-structure-formulas.ss:57-67), which is average(local support,
# activation).  It lives in the builtins now because all three bond scouts call
# it, and the two top-down ones used to hardcode letter-category instead.
bond_facet = choose_bond_facet(obj, neighbor)
if bond_facet is None:
    fizzle()

obj_desc = obj.get_descriptor_for(bond_facet)
neighbor_desc = neighbor.get_descriptor_for(bond_facet)
if obj_desc is None or neighbor_desc is None:
    fizzle()

# Determine bond category
bond_cat = get_bond_category(obj_desc, neighbor_desc)
if bond_cat is None:
    fizzle()

# Determine direction
direction = None
sameness = get_node('plato-sameness')
if bond_cat is not sameness:
    if obj.left_string_pos < neighbor.left_string_pos:
        direction = get_node('plato-right')
    else:
        direction = get_node('plato-left')


# Scheme: every bond scout consults `incompatible-bond-candidates?` before
# proposing (bonds.ss:209, 254, 313).
from server.engine.bonds import incompatible_bond_candidates
if incompatible_bond_candidates(obj, neighbor, bond_facet, bond_cat):
    fizzle()

propose_bond(obj, neighbor, bond_cat, bond_facet, obj_desc, neighbor_desc, direction)

name: top-down-bond-scout:category
description: Top-down scout driven by an active bond-category slipnet node. Chooses a string, picks an object and neighbor, then proposes a bond of the specified category if the descriptors match.
execute_body:
# Top-down bond scout by category
# Scheme: `top-down-bond-scout:category` (bonds.ss:217-266).
bond_cat_node = args.get('slipnode')
if bond_cat_node is None:
    fizzle()

# The string is weighted by average(this category's relevance to it, its average
# intra-string unhappiness), over the non-answer strings (bonds.ss:222-241).
string = choose_string_for(bond_cat_node)
obj = choose_string_object(string, 'intra')
if obj is None:
    fizzle()

neighbor = choose_neighbor(obj)
if neighbor is None:
    fizzle()

bond_facet = choose_bond_facet(obj, neighbor)
if bond_facet is None:
    fizzle()

obj_desc = obj.get_descriptor_for(bond_facet)
neighbor_desc = neighbor.get_descriptor_for(bond_facet)
if obj_desc is None or neighbor_desc is None:
    fizzle()

# Scheme: every bond scout consults `incompatible-bond-candidates?` before
# proposing (bonds.ss:209, 254, 313).
from server.engine.bonds import incompatible_bond_candidates
if incompatible_bond_candidates(obj, neighbor, bond_facet, bond_cat_node):
    fizzle()

# Both descriptor orders (bonds.ss:258-263).  Drawing `c` with neighbour `b`
# while hunting successor *is* a successor bond -- b->c -- and testing only
# (obj, neighbour) threw half of every category scout's work away.
if get_bond_category(obj_desc, neighbor_desc) is bond_cat_node:
    from_obj, to_obj = obj, neighbor
    from_desc, to_desc = obj_desc, neighbor_desc
elif get_bond_category(neighbor_desc, obj_desc) is bond_cat_node:
    from_obj, to_obj = neighbor, obj
    from_desc, to_desc = neighbor_desc, obj_desc
else:
    fizzle()

direction = None
if bond_cat_node is not get_node('plato-sameness'):
    if from_obj.left_string_pos < to_obj.left_string_pos:
        direction = get_node('plato-right')
    else:
        direction = get_node('plato-left')

propose_bond(from_obj, to_obj, bond_cat_node, bond_facet, from_desc, to_desc, direction)

name: top-down-bond-scout:direction
description: Top-down scout driven by an active direction slipnet node. Chooses a string, picks an object, selects the neighbor in the specified direction, and proposes a directed bond.
execute_body:
# Top-down bond scout by direction
# Scheme: `top-down-bond-scout:direction` (bonds.ss:269-318).
dir_node = args.get('slipnode')
if dir_node is None:
    fizzle()

# The string is weighted by average(this direction's relevance to it, its average
# intra-string unhappiness), over the non-answer strings (bonds.ss:274-293).
string = choose_string_for(dir_node)
obj = choose_string_object(string, 'intra')
if obj is None:
    fizzle()

# `choose-left-neighbor` / `choose-right-neighbor` (bonds.ss:295-297): the
# adjacent letter -- even inside a group -- plus every group edged there, picked
# by intra-string salience.  `get_object_at` returned the letter and nothing else.
neighbor_obj = choose_directed_neighbor(obj, dir_node)
if neighbor_obj is None:
    fizzle()

bond_facet = choose_bond_facet(obj, neighbor_obj)
if bond_facet is None:
    fizzle()

obj_desc = obj.get_descriptor_for(bond_facet)
neighbor_desc = neighbor_obj.get_descriptor_for(bond_facet)
if obj_desc is None or neighbor_desc is None:
    fizzle()

bond_cat = get_bond_category(obj_desc, neighbor_desc)
if bond_cat is None or bond_cat is get_node('plato-sameness'):
    fizzle()


# Scheme: every bond scout consults `incompatible-bond-candidates?` before
# proposing (bonds.ss:209, 254, 313).
from server.engine.bonds import incompatible_bond_candidates
if incompatible_bond_candidates(obj, neighbor_obj, bond_facet, bond_cat):
    fizzle()

propose_bond(obj, neighbor_obj, bond_cat, bond_facet, obj_desc, neighbor_desc, dir_node)

name: bond-evaluator
description: Evaluates a proposed bond's strength and probabilistically accepts or rejects it.
execute_body:
# Bond evaluator
bond = args.get('structure')
if bond is None:
    fizzle()

if not evaluate_structure(bond):
    fizzle()

# Scheme: bond-evaluator re-activates the descriptors and facet (bonds.ss:346-349)
activate_from_workspace(bond.from_descriptor, bond.to_descriptor, bond.bond_facet)

post_codelet('bond-builder', round(bond.strength), structure=bond)

name: bond-builder
description: Attempts to build an evaluated bond. Fights incompatible structures, breaks losers, builds the bond.
execute_body:
# Bond builder
bond = args.get('structure')
if bond is None:
    fizzle()

# Verify objects still exist in workspace
if bond.from_object.string is None or bond.to_object.string is None:
    fizzle()

# The category and direction are jolted by `build-bond` (bonds.ss:419-421) and,
# when the bond turns out to be a duplicate, by the duplicate branch
# (bonds.ss:366-368) -- both of which are inside `build_structure`.  Jolting them
# here as well jolted them after a *lost fight* too, which the Scheme never does:
# a bond that loses to what is already built has said nothing new about the
# string, and should not warm its category as though it had.
build_structure(bond)

name: top-down-group-scout:category
description: Top-down scout driven by an active group-category slipnet node. Chooses a string, picks an object, scans adjacent bonds matching the group category, and proposes a group.
execute_body:
# Top-down group scout by category
# Scheme: groups.ss:418-486 -- pick a scan direction, then scan-bonds that way.
from server.engine.groups import Group

grp_cat_node = args.get('slipnode')
if grp_cat_node is None:
    fizzle()

# The bond category this group category is built from.
bond_cat = None
for lk in grp_cat_node.lateral_links:
    if lk.label_node and lk.label_node.name == 'plato-bond-category':
        bond_cat = lk.to_node
        break
if bond_cat is None:
    fizzle()

string = choose_string()
if not string.bonds:
    fizzle()

obj = choose_string_object(string, 'intra')
if obj is None:
    fizzle()

# A whole-string object has nothing left to group.
if obj.spans_whole_string():
    fizzle()

# Scan left or right, not always right: the leftmost object can only scan right
# and the rightmost only left, and otherwise the choice follows the activations
# of plato-left / plato-right.  Scanning rightwards only meant a group could be
# found from just one of its ends, which biased which groups ever formed.
left_node = get_node('plato-left')
right_node = get_node('plato-right')
if obj.left_bond is None and obj.right_bond is not None:
    scan_right = True
elif obj.right_bond is None and obj.left_bond is not None:
    scan_right = False
else:
    scan_right = weighted_pick(
        [True, False],
        [right_node.activation, left_node.activation],
    )

initial_bond = obj.right_bond if scan_right else obj.left_bond
if initial_bond is None or not initial_bond.is_built or initial_bond.bond_category is not bond_cat:
    # Scheme: groups.ss:466-486.  No matching bond to scan, so instead wrap a
    # lone *letter* in a singleton group -- a group of length one.  This is what
    # lets `m` in `mrrjjj` become a length-one group and bond to `rr`
    # (length two) on the Length facet, giving the 1-2-3 reading behind the
    # answer mrrjjjj (S5.2.1 Run 1).  A group cannot be made singleton.
    if obj.spans_whole_string() or hasattr(obj, 'objects'):
        fizzle()
    singleton_direction = None
    if grp_cat_node.name != 'plato-samegrp':
        singleton_direction = weighted_pick(
            [left_node, right_node],
            [
                descriptor_support(string, 'plato-left'),
                descriptor_support(string, 'plato-right'),
            ],
        )
    singleton = Group(
        string, grp_cat_node, get_node('plato-letter-category'),
        singleton_direction, [obj], [],
    )
    if not prob(single_letter_group_probability(singleton)):
        fizzle()
    singleton.time_stamp = codelet_count
    post_codelet('group-evaluator', round(grp_cat_node.activation), structure=singleton)
    fizzle()

# Scan limit from the string's bond-scan distribution.
max_scan = rng.randint(string.length) + 1

objects = [obj]
bonds = []
current = obj
for _scan in range(max_scan):
    b = current.right_bond if scan_right else current.left_bond
    if b is None or not b.is_built:
        break
    if b.bond_category is not bond_cat:
        break
    nxt = b.right_object if scan_right else b.left_object
    if nxt is None or nxt is current or nxt in objects:
        break
    objects.append(nxt)
    bonds.append(b)
    current = nxt

if len(objects) < 2:
    fizzle()

objects.sort(key=lambda o: o.left_string_pos)
direction = bonds[0].direction
bond_facet = bonds[0].bond_facet

group = Group(string, grp_cat_node, bond_facet, direction, objects, bonds)
group.time_stamp = codelet_count
post_codelet('group-evaluator', round(grp_cat_node.activation), structure=group)

name: top-down-group-scout:direction
description: Top-down scout driven by an active direction slipnet node. Chooses a string, picks an object, scans bonds in the specified direction, and proposes a group.
execute_body:
# Top-down group scout by direction
# Scheme: groups.ss:489-544 — uses scan-bonds with count limit
from server.engine.groups import Group

dir_node = args.get('slipnode')
if dir_node is None:
    fizzle()

string = choose_string()
if not string.bonds:
    fizzle()

obj = choose_string_object(string, 'intra')
if obj is None:
    fizzle()

# Find initial bond in specified direction
initial_bond = None
if dir_node.name == 'plato-right' and obj.right_bond and obj.right_bond.is_built:
    if obj.right_bond.direction is dir_node:
        initial_bond = obj.right_bond
elif dir_node.name == 'plato-left' and obj.left_bond and obj.left_bond.is_built:
    if obj.left_bond.direction is dir_node:
        initial_bond = obj.left_bond

if initial_bond is None:
    fizzle()

bond_cat = initial_bond.bond_category
objects = [obj]
bonds = [initial_bond]
current = initial_bond.right_object if dir_node.name == 'plato-right' else initial_bond.left_object
objects.append(current)

# Count-limited scan (Scheme: scan-bonds with max-num-to-scan)
max_scan = rng.randint(string.length) + 1
for _scan in range(max_scan):
    next_bond = current.right_bond if dir_node.name == 'plato-right' else current.left_bond
    if next_bond is None or not next_bond.is_built:
        break
    if next_bond.bond_category is not bond_cat or next_bond.direction is not dir_node:
        break
    next_obj = next_bond.right_object if dir_node.name == 'plato-right' else next_bond.left_object
    objects.append(next_obj)
    bonds.append(next_bond)
    current = next_obj

if len(objects) < 2:
    fizzle()

# Find group category from bond category
grp_cat = None
for lk in bond_cat.lateral_links:
    if lk.label_node and lk.label_node.name == 'plato-group-category':
        grp_cat = lk.to_node
        break
if grp_cat is None:
    fizzle()

bond_facet = bonds[0].bond_facet
group = Group(string, grp_cat, bond_facet, dir_node, objects, bonds)
group.time_stamp = codelet_count
post_codelet('group-evaluator', round(dir_node.activation), structure=group)

name: group-scout:whole-string
description: Bottom-up scout that attempts to form a group spanning an entire string.
execute_body:
# Whole-string group scout
# Scheme: groups.ss:545-580 — walks bonds from leftmost to rightmost
from server.engine.groups import Group

string = choose_string()
if not string.bonds:
    fizzle()

# Check if bonds span the whole string
letters = string.letters
if len(letters) < 2:
    fizzle()

# Walk right bonds from leftmost letter (bounded by string length)
objects = [letters[0]]
bonds = []
current = letters[0]
for _scan in range(string.length):
    b = current.right_bond
    if b is None or not b.is_built:
        break
    objects.append(b.right_object)
    bonds.append(b)
    current = b.right_object
    if current is letters[-1]:
        break

if current is not letters[-1] or len(bonds) == 0:
    fizzle()

# Check all bonds have same category
first_cat = bonds[0].bond_category
if not all(b.bond_category is first_cat for b in bonds):
    fizzle()

direction = bonds[0].direction
bond_facet = bonds[0].bond_facet

# Find group category
grp_cat = None
for lk in first_cat.lateral_links:
    if lk.label_node and lk.label_node.name == 'plato-group-category':
        grp_cat = lk.to_node
        break
if grp_cat is None:
    fizzle()

group = Group(string, grp_cat, bond_facet, direction, objects, bonds)
group.time_stamp = codelet_count
post_codelet('group-evaluator', 35, structure=group)

description: Attempts to build an evaluated group.
execute_body:

name: bottom-up-bridge-scout
description: Randomly selects a bridge type weighted by inverse mapping strength, chooses two objects, computes concept-mappings, and proposes a bridge.
execute_body:
# Bottom-up bridge scout
from server.engine.bridges import Bridge, BRIDGE_TOP, BRIDGE_BOTTOM, BRIDGE_VERTICAL
from server.engine.bridges import make_concept_mappings

# Choose bridge type weighted by inverse mapping strength
types_and_strings = [('top', BRIDGE_TOP, workspace.initial_string, workspace.modified_string)]
types_and_strings.append(('vertical', BRIDGE_VERTICAL, workspace.initial_string, workspace.target_string))
if justify_mode:
    types_and_strings.append(('bottom', BRIDGE_BOTTOM, workspace.target_string, workspace.answer_string))

weights = [100 - mapping_strength(t[0]) for t in types_and_strings]
chosen = weighted_pick(types_and_strings, weights)
bt_name, bt, string1, string2 = chosen

if string2 is None:
    fizzle()

# Choose objects from each string weighted by inter-string salience
key = 'horizontal_inter' if bt != BRIDGE_VERTICAL else 'vertical_inter'
obj1 = choose_string_object(string1, key)
obj2 = choose_string_object(string2, key)
if obj1 is None or obj2 is None:
    fizzle()

# Compute concept mappings, honouring the horizontal/vertical asymmetry (S3.3.1)
# One object spanning its whole string while the other does not is not a
# correspondence worth pursuing (Scheme: lone-spanning-object?).
if obj1.spans_whole_string() != obj2.spans_whole_string():
    fizzle()

cms = make_concept_mappings(obj1, obj2, bt, get_node('plato-identity'))

if not cms:
    fizzle()

bridge = Bridge(obj1, obj2, bt, cms)
bridge.time_stamp = codelet_count
avg_strength = sum(cm.strength() for cm in cms) / len(cms)
post_codelet('bridge-evaluator', round(avg_strength), structure=bridge)

name: important-object-bridge-scout
description: Selects a bridge type, chooses object1 by relative importance, finds a matching object2 via distinguishing descriptions.
execute_body:
# Important-object bridge scout
# Scheme: important-object-bridge-scout (bridges.ss:966-1030).
from server.engine.bridges import Bridge, BRIDGE_TOP, BRIDGE_BOTTOM, BRIDGE_VERTICAL
from server.engine.bridges import make_concept_mappings

types_and_strings = [('top', BRIDGE_TOP, workspace.initial_string, workspace.modified_string)]
types_and_strings.append(('vertical', BRIDGE_VERTICAL, workspace.initial_string, workspace.target_string))
if justify_mode:
    types_and_strings.append(('bottom', BRIDGE_BOTTOM, workspace.target_string, workspace.answer_string))

weights = [100 - mapping_strength(t[0]) for t in types_and_strings]
bt_name, bt, string1, string2 = weighted_pick(types_and_strings, weights)
if string2 is None:
    fizzle()

# Choose object1 by relative importance, then one of its relevant
# distinguishing descriptions, weighted by conceptual depth.
obj1 = choose_string_object(string1, 'relative_importance')
if obj1 is None:
    fizzle()

relevant = obj1.get_relevant_distinguishing_descriptions()
if not relevant:
    fizzle()
chosen_desc = weighted_pick(relevant, [d.descriptor.conceptual_depth for d in relevant])
obj1_descriptor = chosen_desc.descriptor

# If the mapping already slips this descriptor to another, look for *that*
# descriptor on the far side.  This is how an established interpretation
# propagates itself across the rest of the mapping.
obj2_descriptor = obj1_descriptor
for slippage in workspace.get_all_slippages(bt_name):
    if slippage.descriptor1 is obj1_descriptor:
        obj2_descriptor = slippage.descriptor2
        break

# Every object carrying that descriptor is a candidate -- then choose among them
# by inter-string salience.  Taking the first match in list order instead meant
# letters (which precede groups in `objects`) always won, so a bridge from a
# letter to a *group* was essentially unreachable: c could never be seen as
# corresponding to the jjj group, only to the rightmost j.  That is the
# difference between the answers mrrkkk and mrrjjk (S1.5).
key = 'horizontal_inter' if bt != BRIDGE_VERTICAL else 'vertical_inter'
candidates = []
for candidate in string2.objects:
    for d2 in candidate.get_relevant_descriptions():
        if d2.descriptor is obj2_descriptor:
            candidates.append(candidate)
            break
if not candidates:
    fizzle()

obj2 = weighted_pick(candidates, [c.salience.get(key, 1.0) for c in candidates])

# One object spanning its whole string while the other does not is not a
# correspondence worth pursuing (Scheme: lone-spanning-object?).
if obj1.spans_whole_string() != obj2.spans_whole_string():
    fizzle()

cms = make_concept_mappings(obj1, obj2, bt, get_node('plato-identity'))
if not cms:
    fizzle()

bridge = Bridge(obj1, obj2, bt, cms)
bridge.time_stamp = codelet_count
avg_strength = sum(cm.strength() for cm in cms) / len(cms)
post_codelet('bridge-evaluator', round(avg_strength), structure=bridge)

name: bridge-builder
description: Builds an evaluated bridge into the workspace.
execute_body:
# Bridge builder
bridge = args.get('structure')
if bridge is None:
    fizzle()

# Verify both objects still exist
if bridge.object1.string is None or bridge.object2.string is None:
    fizzle()

build_structure(bridge)

# Scheme: concept-mappings activate their description types, descriptors and
# labels when a bridge is built (concept-mappings.ss:161-171).
for cm in bridge.concept_mappings:
    cm.activate_descriptions()
    cm.activate_label()

name: bottom-up-description-scout
description: Chooses an object, selects a relevant description, follows property links, and proposes a new description.
execute_body:
# Bottom-up description scout (descriptions.ss:105-124)
#
# Object choice is by *average* salience -- the measure that folds intra-string
# salience together with the inter-string ones -- because a description is
# equally useful to bonds within a string and to bridges across strings, so
# neither view of attention should decide alone.
obj = choose_object('average')
if obj is None:
    fizzle()

# `choose-relevant-description-by-activation` (workspace-objects.ss:603-609):
# relevant means the description *type* is fully active, and among those the
# descriptor's own activation decides.
relevant = [d for d in obj.descriptions if d.is_relevant()]
if not relevant:
    fizzle()

weights = [d.descriptor.activation for d in relevant]
chosen = weighted_pick(relevant, weights)

# Not every property link is worth following: each survives with probability
# equal to its degree of association, temperature-adjusted (slipnet.ss:108-112).
# The two shipped links, a=>first and z=>last, are association 25, so `first`
# and `last` enter the Workspace at roughly the rate the reference admits them
# rather than on every scout that reaches here.
property_links = chosen.descriptor.get_similar_property_links(
    rng, temperature.value, meta
)
if not property_links:
    fizzle()

# And among the survivors, association times how active the property already is.
properties = [lk.to_node for lk in property_links]
weights = [lk.degree_of_association() * lk.to_node.activation
           for lk in property_links]
chosen_property = weighted_pick(properties, weights)

new_desc_type = chosen_property.category
if new_desc_type is None:
    fizzle()

# No duplicate pre-check: a description that already exists still travels to the
# builder, which re-activates the type and the descriptor before it fizzles
# (descriptions.ss:164-168).  That stream of re-activation is what holds a
# concept up against decay once the Workspace has committed to it.
propose_description(obj, new_desc_type, chosen_property)

name: top-down-description-scout
description: Top-down scout driven by an active description-type slipnet node. Chooses an object and proposes a description of the specified type.
execute_body:
# Top-down description scout (descriptions.ss:127-140)
desc_type_node = args.get('slipnode')
if desc_type_node is None:
    fizzle()

# Average salience, as in the bottom-up scout: `(tell scope 'choose-object
# 'get-average-salience)`.
obj = choose_object('average')
if obj is None:
    fizzle()

# Only descriptors that genuinely apply to the object are candidates
# (Scheme: get-possible-descriptors / define-descriptor-predicate), picked
# stochastically by activation.
descriptor = possible_descriptor(obj, desc_type_node.name)
if descriptor is None:
    fizzle()

# The reference does not ask whether the object already carries a description of
# this type -- and asking is worse than redundant, because the answer that
# matters is per *descriptor*, not per dimension: an object described as
# `leftmost` would refuse ever to be reconsidered as `whole`.  A duplicate is
# the builder's business, and it re-activates both concepts on the way out
# (descriptions.ss:164-168).
propose_description(obj, desc_type_node, descriptor)

name: description-evaluator
description: Evaluates a proposed description and probabilistically accepts or rejects it.
execute_body:
# Description evaluator
desc = args.get('structure')
if desc is None:
    fizzle()

# Scheme: description-evaluator activates the descriptor (descriptions.ss:146)
activate_from_workspace(desc.descriptor)

if not evaluate_structure(desc):
    fizzle()

post_codelet('description-builder', round(desc.strength), structure=desc)

name: description-builder
description: Builds an evaluated description by attaching it to its object.
execute_body:
# Description builder
desc = args.get('structure')
if desc is None:
    fizzle()

if desc.object is None or desc.object.string is None:
    fizzle()

# Already present: still worth re-activating the concepts (descriptions.ss:165-168)
for d in desc.object.descriptions:
    if d.description_type is desc.description_type and d.descriptor is desc.descriptor:
        activate_from_workspace(desc.description_type, desc.descriptor)
        fizzle()

build_structure(desc)

# Scheme: build-description activates type and descriptor (descriptions.ss:189-191)
activate_from_workspace(desc.description_type, desc.descriptor)

name: rule-scout
description: Discovers transformation rules by examining horizontal bridges.
execute_body:
# Rule scout (S3.3.6; rules.ss:397-442)
#
# Abstract a rule from the slippages underlying a horizontal mapping.  This runs
# the real abstraction pipeline: intrinsic changes from individual slippages,
# extrinsic changes from symmetries, "all components of X" changes, then the
# rule-abstraction heuristics that sieve out redundant changes.
from server.engine.rules import build_rule_from_bridges, RULE_TOP, RULE_BOTTOM, Rule, RuleClause, CLAUSE_VERBATIM

# rules.ss:399-412.  The verbatim branch is drawn FIRST and unconditionally, at
# 1%, whatever the workspace looks like: S3.3.6's "some (small) chance that the
# codelet will simply ignore the bridges".  It is not a fallback for having no
# bridges -- taking it whenever the bridge set was empty meant a verbatim rule
# with probability 1 for the whole early run, and a verbatim top rule is
# vacuously supported, so it opened the answer-finder gate and translated
# straight into the modified string as an answer.
verbatim_probability = meta.get_param('verbatim_rule_probability', 0.01)
if prob(verbatim_probability):
    rule_type = rng.pick([RULE_TOP, RULE_BOTTOM]) if justify_mode else RULE_TOP
    result_string = workspace.modified_string if rule_type == RULE_TOP else workspace.answer_string
    if result_string is None:
        fizzle()
    letters = [get_node('plato-' + ch) for ch in result_string.text]
    if any(l is None for l in letters):
        fizzle()
    rule = Rule(rule_type, [RuleClause(clause_type=CLAUSE_VERBATIM, verbatim_letters=letters)])
    rule.set_verbatim_rule_information()
    rule.time_stamp = codelet_count
    rule.compute_quality(meta)
    rule.transcribe_to_english()
    post_codelet('rule-evaluator', round(max(1, rule.quality)), structure=rule)
    fizzle()

# rules.ss:413-416.  Otherwise a rule has to actually be POSSIBLE: every letter of
# both strings of the pair covered by rule-describable bridges.  Without the gate,
# rules were abstracted from whatever partial bridge set happened to exist -- "change
# the rightmost letter to d" from a lone c-d bridge, long before the reference
# allows any rule at all.  The flags are set once per update cycle by
# check_if_rules_possible (run.ss:305), so a scout reads the last cycle's verdict.
possible_rule_types = workspace.get_possible_rule_types()
if not possible_rule_types:
    fizzle()

rule_type = rng.pick(possible_rule_types)
rule = build_rule_from_bridges(
    rule_type, get_built_bridges(rule_type), slipnet,
    rng=rng, temperature=temperature.value, themespace=themespace, meta=meta,
)
if rule is None:
    fizzle()

rule.time_stamp = codelet_count
rule.compute_quality(meta)
rule.transcribe_to_english()

post_codelet('rule-evaluator', round(max(1, rule.quality)), structure=rule)

name: rule-evaluator
description: Evaluates a proposed rule and probabilistically accepts or rejects it.
execute_body:
# Rule evaluator (S3.3.6)
#
# "determines (1) whether or not the rule actually works (that is, whether
# applying the rule to the initial string really does produce the modified
# string), and (2) whether the rule is of high enough quality to actually merit
# building."
rule = args.get('structure')
if rule is None:
    fizzle()

if not rule.currently_works(workspace, slipnet):
    fizzle()

if not evaluate_structure(rule):
    fizzle()

post_codelet('rule-builder', round(max(1, rule.quality)), structure=rule)

name: rule-builder
description: Builds a rule and posts an answer-finder.
execute_body:
# Rule builder
#
# Unlike Copycat, building a rule does not require destroying an existing one:
# "many different rules can coexist in Metacat's Workspace" (S3.3.6 footnote 4).
rule = args.get('structure')
if rule is None:
    fizzle()

# Don't accumulate duplicates of a rule we already have.
existing = workspace.top_rules if rule.is_top_rule else workspace.bottom_rules
for other in existing:
    if other is not rule and other.rules_equal(rule):
        fizzle()

build_structure(rule)

# The concepts making up a rule are activated by its creation.
for node, _act in rule.get_concept_pattern():
    activate_from_workspace(node)

name: answer-finder
description: Attempts to produce an answer by translating a top rule across the vertical mapping.
execute_body:
# Answer finder (S3.4)
# Scheme: answers.ss:928-1000, step for step.
from server.engine.answers import compute_answer_quality
from server.engine.formulas import temp_adjusted_values

# Codelets "probabilistically decide whether or not to attempt answer creation on
# the basis of the overall strengths of the horizontal and vertical mappings
# between strings (as long as these mappings are weak, codelets are unlikely to
# try)."  Scheme: (stochastic-if* (1- (^3 (* (% top-strength) (% vertical-strength)))))
# -- a graded discouragement, not a threshold.
top_strength = mapping_strength('top')
vert_strength = mapping_strength('vertical')
if prob(1.0 - ((top_strength / 100.0) * (vert_strength / 100.0)) ** 3):
    fizzle()

supported = workspace.get_supported_rules(True)
if not supported:
    fizzle()

# Rules are picked by temperature-adjusted *strength* (answers.ss:943-945); a rule's
# internal strength is its relative quality (rules.ss:286).
weights = temp_adjusted_values([r.strength for r in supported], temperature.value, meta)
if not any(weights):
    fizzle()
chosen_rule = weighted_pick(supported, weights)

# A separate gate on how well the Workspace still supports the rule that was picked
# (answers.ss:946-950).  Vacuously 100 for a rule resting on no bridges.
if prob(1.0 - chosen_rule.get_degree_of_support(workspace) / 100.0):
    fizzle()

# "Chosen rule no longer works" (answers.ss:951-953).
if not chosen_rule.currently_works(workspace, slipnet):
    fizzle()

translated = translate_rule(chosen_rule)
if translated is None:
    fizzle()

answer_text = apply_rule(translated)
if answer_text is None:
    # A snag: the translated rule cannot be applied to the target string.
    record_snag(chosen_rule, translated)
    fizzle()

# "Already found this answer. Fizzling." (answers.ss:982) -- consult Episodic
# Memory before reporting so the search carries on toward a DIFFERENT answer
# rather than rediscovering one already stored.
if answer_present(answer_text, chosen_rule, translated):
    fizzle()

quality = compute_answer_quality(chosen_rule.quality, temperature.value, meta)
report_answer(
    answer_text, quality,
    top_rule=chosen_rule,
    bottom_rule=translated,
    unjustified_slippages=getattr(translated, 'unjustified_slippages', []),
)

name: answer-justifier
description: Used in justify mode to validate a given answer.
execute_body:
# Answer justifier (S4.3.1)
#
# Choose a top or bottom rule, translate it through the vertical mapping, and
# see whether the result matches (or can be made to match) a rule describing the
# other string pair.  When it almost fits, clamp patterns to force the Workspace
# to reorganise; when a pair of rules can be unified, clamp the vertical themes
# the unification implies.
from server.engine.justify import attempt_justification
from server.engine.answers import compute_answer_quality

if not justify_mode:
    fizzle()

# The coderack goes in because a justify clamp clamps codelet patterns as well as
# themes and concepts (justify.ss:167-172); the clamp event applies all three, so
# there is nothing left for this body to apply afterwards.
result = attempt_justification(
    workspace, meta, rng,
    trace=trace, themespace=themespace, slipnet=slipnet, memory=memory,
    codelet_count=codelet_count, temperature=temperature.value,
    coderack=coderack, temperature_control=temperature,
)

if result.justified:
    quality = compute_answer_quality(result.quality, temperature.value, meta)
    report_answer(
        workspace.answer_string.text, quality,
        top_rule=result.top_rule, bottom_rule=result.bottom_rule,
        unjustified_slippages=result.unjustified_slippages,
    )
else:
    fizzle()

name: thematic-bridge-scout
description: Self-watching codelet that scouts for bridges guided by active Themespace themes.
execute_body:
# Thematic bridge scout (S4.1.2)
#
# The third channel of top-down thematic pressure: seek a bridge that satisfies a
# *conjunction* of positively-activated themes at once, and propose the
# descriptions that would make such a bridge expressible.  S4.1.2 is explicit
# about the conjunction -- "if the top themes Letter-Category: identity and
# String-Position: different are both active, thematic-scout codelets will tend
# to look for potential bridges ... having the same letter-category but different
# string positions" -- and the crosswise mapping of S2.4.5 is exactly such a
# conjunction.
#
# Negative themes are deliberately ignored here.  They exert pressure only
# through structure strength, because scouting on them would "result in a tangle
# of proposed bridges ... most of which would contribute little or nothing to the
# emergence of a coherent mapping" (p.144, themes.ss:771-775).
from server.engine.bridges import propose_bridge
from server.engine.themes import (
    bridge_orientation,
    bridge_type_for_theme_type,
    conditions_for_bridge,
    look_for_auxiliary_slippages,
    pick_theme_conjunction,
    pick_theme_type,
    propose_description_based_on_theme,
)

if not self_watching:
    fizzle()

# Which mapping to scout: how loudly that type's themes are speaking, times how
# much room is left in the mapping (themes.ss:760-768).
theme_type = pick_theme_type(themespace, workspace, rng)
if theme_type is None:
    fizzle()

bridge_type = bridge_type_for_theme_type(theme_type)
orientation = bridge_orientation(bridge_type)

themes = pick_theme_conjunction(themespace, theme_type, rng)
if not themes:
    fizzle()

objects = workspace.get_possible_bridge_objects(bridge_type)
if not objects:
    fizzle()

salience_key = 'horizontal_inter' if orientation == 'horizontal' else 'vertical_inter'
chosen_object = weighted_pick(
    objects, [o.salience.get(salience_key, 1.0) for o in objects]
)
chosen_string = chosen_object.string

applicable = [
    t for t in themes if object_has_description_type(chosen_object, t.dimension)
]
non_applicable = [t for t in themes if t not in applicable]

# A theme naming a dimension the chosen object has no description along is a
# reason to look for one, not a reason to give up: "situations tend to be
# perceived in terms of the features that one is actively paying attention to"
# (p.144).  The one exception is String-Position -- if no position description is
# possible for the object at all, a bridge with it would be spurious, and without
# this test iijjkk->aabbdd with StringPos and ObjCtgy clamped proposes i--b
# bridges (themes.ss:820-829).
for theme in non_applicable:
    if theme.dimension == 'plato-string-position-category' and not get_node(
        'plato-string-position-category'
    ).description_possible(chosen_object):
        fizzle()
    description = propose_description_based_on_theme(
        chosen_object, theme, slipnet, rng
    )
    if description is not None:
        post_codelet(
            'description-evaluator',
            max(1, round(abs(theme.activation))),
            structure=description,
        )

other_string = workspace.get_other_string(chosen_string, orientation)
if other_string is None:
    fizzle()

# The counterpart has to carry *every* applicable dimension already: without a
# description along a dimension there is nothing for that theme to be true or
# false of, so the conjunction could not be judged (themes.ss:834-837).
other_candidates = [
    o for o in other_string.objects
    if all(object_has_description_type(o, t.dimension) for t in applicable)
]
if not other_candidates:
    fizzle()

from_object = chosen_string.string_type == 'initial' or (
    chosen_string.string_type == 'target' and orientation == 'horizontal'
)
get_conditions = conditions_for_bridge(chosen_object, from_object, applicable, rng)

selection = []
for candidate in other_candidates:
    conditions = get_conditions(candidate)
    if conditions is None:
        continue
    selection.append(
        (candidate.salience.get(salience_key, 1.0), candidate, conditions)
    )
if not selection:
    fizzle()

_weight, other_object, conditions = weighted_pick(
    selection, [entry[0] for entry in selection]
)
object1 = chosen_object if from_object else other_object
object2 = other_object if from_object else chosen_object

bridge = propose_bridge(
    bridge_type,
    object1, any(o is object1 for o in conditions),
    object2, any(o is object2 for o in conditions),
    get_node('plato-identity'),
)
bridge.time_stamp = codelet_count

# S3.4.1: a slippage the bridge already carries can drag a related one along on
# its coattails -- leftmost=>rightmost pulling right=>left.  When an object
# cannot yet be described in the new dimension the Scheme builds that description
# and stops there (themes.ss:933-948): the description was the useful work, and a
# later codelet can find the slippage.
description = look_for_auxiliary_slippages(bridge, slipnet, rng)
if description is not None:
    build_structure(description)
    fizzle()

# themes.ss:880-886 -- the more strongly the satisfied themes are activated, the
# more urgently the bridge is pursued, and a whole-string object is the most
# urgent of all because a spanning bridge organises everything under it.
urgency = round(
    (max(t.activation for t in applicable) / 100.0)
    * (
        meta.get_urgency('extremely_high')
        if chosen_object.string_spanning_group()
        else meta.get_urgency('very_high')
    )
)
post_codelet('bridge-evaluator', max(1, urgency), structure=bridge)

name: progress-watcher
description: Self-watching codelet that monitors system progress.
execute_body:
# Progress watcher (S4.5.1)
from server.engine.jootsing import check_progress
from server.engine.commentary import emit_clamp_expired

if not self_watching:
    fizzle()

result = check_progress(
    workspace, trace, codelet_count, meta,
    commentary=commentary,
    justify_mode=justify_mode,
    self_watching_enabled=self_watching,
    rng=rng,
    themespace=themespace,
    slipnet=slipnet,
    coderack=coderack,
    temperature_control=temperature,
)

if result.action in ('undo_clamp', 'post_answer_finder', 'post_answer_justifier'):
    # The clamp period has run its course.
    if trace.within_clamp_period:
        emit_clamp_expired(commentary, 'clamp', result.progress_value, codelet_count)
        trace.within_clamp_period = False
        trace.last_unclamp_time = codelet_count
        coderack.unclamp_all()
        themespace.unclamp_all()

if result.action in ('post_answer_finder', 'post_answer_justifier'):
    # jootsing.ss:266-271: urgency IS the progress achieved under the clamp -- the
    # more the clamp accomplished, the more insistently the answer stage is tried.
    # Deriving it from the temperature instead made the urgency a fact about the
    # whole run rather than about this clamp.
    urgency = max(1, round(result.progress_value))
    post_codelet('answer-justifier' if justify_mode else 'answer-finder', urgency)
elif result.action == 'clamp_rule_pattern':
    pattern = meta.codelet_patterns.get('rule-codelet-pattern', [])
    if pattern:
        coderack.clamp_pattern(pattern)

name: jootser
description: Self-watching codelet that detects and escapes repetitive failure patterns (Jumping Out Of The System).
execute_body:
# Jootser (S4.5.2)
from server.engine.jootsing import attempt_jootsing
from server.engine.answers import compute_answer_quality

if not self_watching:
    fizzle()

result = attempt_jootsing(
    trace, themespace, meta,
    commentary=commentary,
    codelet_count=codelet_count,
    self_watching_enabled=self_watching,
    rng=rng,
    slipnet=slipnet,
    workspace=workspace,
    memory=memory,
    coderack=coderack,
    temperature_control=temperature,
)

if result.action == 'post_answer_justifier':
    # jootsing.ss:216-219.  The translated top rule and the bottom rule already say
    # the same thing, so one more push at the justification, at extremely-high
    # urgency.  This outcome used to match no branch at all, and nothing happened.
    post_codelet('answer-justifier', meta.get_urgency('extremely_high'))
elif result.action == 'report_unjustified_answer':
    # jootsing.ss:223-235.  "Giving up" in justify mode means settling for the
    # answer while carrying the slippages it cannot account for -- "Settled for
    # unjustified answer" (trace.ss:435).  This used to terminate the run instead,
    # so where Metacat produces an answer Petacat produced nothing.
    quality = compute_answer_quality(result.answer_quality, temperature.value, meta)
    report_answer(
        workspace.answer_string.text, quality,
        top_rule=result.top_rule, bottom_rule=result.bottom_rule,
        unjustified_slippages=result.unjustified_slippages,
    )
elif result.give_up:
    # Recurring rule-codelet or snag-response clamps (jootsing.ss:173-186): the
    # program stops rather than keep looping.
    give_up()
elif result.pattern_detected and result.negative_pattern:
    # Clamp the negative vertical theme-pattern characterising the recurring
    # snag, plus a bottom-up codelet-pattern to accelerate the search for an
    # alternative interpretation.
    themespace.clamp_negative_pattern(result.negative_pattern)
    pattern = meta.codelet_patterns.get('bottom-up-codelet-pattern', [])
    if pattern:
        coderack.clamp_pattern(pattern)

name: breaker
description: Randomly breaks existing structures to allow restructuring. Probabilistically fizzles at low temperature.
execute_body:
# Breaker codelet
# Probabilistically fizzle at low temperature (prefer to break at high temp)
if not prob(temperature.value / 100.0):
    fizzle()

# Get all built non-rule structures
structures = [s for s in workspace.all_structures
              if hasattr(s, 'is_built') and s.is_built
              and not hasattr(s, 'is_top_rule')]
if not structures:
    fizzle()

# Choose a structure randomly
target = rng.pick(structures)

# Probabilistically break based on weakness (temperature-adjusted)
weakness = target.weakness() / 100.0
break_prob = temp_adjusted_prob(weakness)
if prob(break_prob):
    break_structure(target)
